patients.summary: Healthy college student who joined the practice at 19. Two reflex fainting episodes a year apart, both seen in an outside ED with normal exams and ECGs; the second came after her last practice visit and reached the chart only by message and late ED record.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is 19, home in Haydenville for the summer, heading back to campus for sophomore year. Has been seeing her pediatrician and was told it was time to move to adult care. Student health plan card on file. No current problems, no meds. Booked new patient physical 8/21 at 9:40. Release form emailed so we can pull her pediatric records.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Juniper is a 19 year old woman establishing adult primary care. Grew up locally and saw a pediatric practice until this summer. Going into her second year of college as a biology major; sings in the college choir and says rehearsals are most of her social life.

No ongoing health problems. Takes nothing daily, no supplements. No drug allergies. Never had surgery. Periods regular.

Family: mother treated for an underactive thyroid, father has high blood pressure. Asked specifically: nobody in the family has died suddenly young or has a known heart rhythm condition.

Social: never smoked, does not drink, no vaping. Lives in a dorm during the year, home with her parents in summer.

ROS: negative across systems. Denies chest pain, fainting, racing heartbeat, shortness of breath with singing or exertion.

Exam: well, relaxed young woman. Vitals in flowsheet, BP in normal range. HEENT unremarkable, TMs clear. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged, no nodes. Heart regular, no murmur, rub or gallop. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin clear. Neuro grossly nonfocal, gait normal. Mood and affect bright. PHQ-2 is 0.

Assessment and plan:
1. Adult preventive care. Healthy. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screens drawn today. Pediatric vaccine record requested; will reconcile when it comes. Flu and COVID shots once the fall vaccine is in; she can come by on a school break. Cervical screening begins at 21, not yet.
2. Reviewed how to reach us from campus by portal or phone.

Next yearly exam in about a year.

documents.title: Screening results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Juniper, both screening tests from yesterday came back negative. These are once-in-adulthood tests, so nothing further is needed. Good luck with the semester.

documents.title: Pediatric practice records
documents.author: pediatrics
documents.body:
Records from prior pediatric practice, 2005 through 2024, 61 pages.

Well-child and adolescent visits yearly with normal growth and development. No chronic diagnoses, no hospitalizations, no surgery. No known drug allergies. No regular medications.

Immunization record: primary infant and childhood series complete including MMR and varicella x2. Adolescent doses: Tdap and first HPV and MenACWY at 11; second HPV the following spring; MenACWY booster at 16; MenB two doses before college.

Last well visit 2024 (age 18): normal exam, sports and camp forms completed.

PCP review: immunizations entered. Nothing outstanding except seasonal flu and COVID.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Home for Thanksgiving. Screening questions negative, feeling well, no prior vaccine reactions. Influenza given L deltoid, COVID given R deltoid, lot numbers in MAR. Waited 15 minutes, no problems. VIS sheets given.

events.reason: fainted while giving a class presentation

reports.text: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No pre-excitation, no QT prolongation. No ST or T wave abnormality.

documents.title: I passed out yesterday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I wanted to let you know I fainted yesterday while I was presenting in class and ended up in the ER. They did an EKG and said it was normal and to follow up with my doctor. I feel totally fine today. Do I need to come in?

documents.title: RE: I passed out yesterday
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Juniper, glad you're feeling okay. Yes, the doctor would like to see you after any ER visit for fainting. I've booked you for Wednesday 6/4 at 2:00. If you faint again, or have chest pain, a pounding or racing heart, or fainting during exercise before then, go back to the ER. Could you sign the release in your inbox so we can get the ER notes?

conditions.label: Syncope
conditions.note: single reflex-type faint during a class presentation; ED ECG normal

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here after an ER visit 5/26 for a faint. ER records not received yet; request faxed again today. History from Juniper:

She was standing at the front of the room for a class presentation and had been anxious about it all morning. Partway in she felt hot, queasy and lightheaded and was sweating through her shirt, then woke up on the floor. Her roommate, who was in the class, told her she was out well under a minute and was talking normally soon after she was laid flat. No tongue bite, no incontinence, no confusion afterward. No injury. The ER told her the heart tracing was normal and sent her home the same afternoon.

No episodes before this one and none since. No chest pain, palpitations or breathlessness, and never any lightheadedness with running or singing. Eating and drinking normally. No meds. No family history of sudden death or rhythm problems (rechecked).

Exam: comfortable. Vitals per flowsheet. Lying and standing pressures checked: no drop in pressure, pulse rise within normal. Heart regular, no murmur at rest or with standing. Lungs clear. Neuro nonfocal. No injury marks.

Assessment: syncope, single episode, with a classic warning phase (warmth, nausea, sweating) in an emotional trigger, quick full recovery, normal ER ECG and normal exam today. Fits a reflex (vasovagal) faint. Nothing here points to a cardiac cause.

Plan:
- CBC and BMP today to make sure there is no anemia or salt problem behind it.
- Talked through triggers: stress, heat, standing still, skipping meals. Keep fluids up, eat before big events.
- When the warning feeling starts: sit or lie down right away, legs up if she can; leg crossing and fist clenching can buy time.
- Return sooner or go to the ER for fainting with exertion, chest pain, a racing heart before passing out, or an injury.
- Will review the ER chart when it arrives.

documents.title: Your blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Juniper, yesterday's labs are all normal: no anemia, and your salts, sugar and kidney numbers are fine. That fits with what we talked about. Keep up the water and the snacks before presentations.

documents.title: Regional hospital ED record, 5/26/2025
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 05/26/2025
Patient: Juniper Foster, 19 F

CC: syncope during a class presentation.

HPI: 19 yo F brought in by her roommate after passing out while speaking in front of her class. Describes being very anxious beforehand. Immediately prior: lightheaded, nauseated, felt overheated, profuse sweating. Roommate reports LOC less than 1 minute with rapid recovery once supine.

PMH: none. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family hx: mother hypothyroidism, father HTN. No FHx of sudden cardiac death or inherited arrhythmia.
Social: college sophomore, biology, choir. Never smoker. No EtOH.

Vitals: BP 120/75, HR 70, afebrile.
Exam: well appearing. CV and full exam unremarkable.
ECG: NSR, no abnormalities.

ED course / impression: syncope with typical prodrome and emotional trigger, benign evaluation.
Disposition: discharged home. Follow up with PCP.

PCP review 7/16: matches her account at the 6/4 visit. Nothing new. Filed.

documents.title: Choir question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! Our fall concert has us standing on risers for about an hour. I haven't fainted again but I'm a little nervous about it. Is there anything I should do?

documents.title: RE: Choir question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. Drink a full bottle of water and eat something salty in the hour before, keep your knees soft rather than locked, and shift your weight or rise on your toes between pieces. If the hot, queasy feeling starts, sit down on the riser even mid-song; your director will understand. Let me know if anything happens.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for seasonal vaccines on a Friday afternoon off from class. Given her history of fainting, vaccines given seated and she stayed seated for the observation period. Flu L deltoid, COVID R deltoid. Felt fine, no lightheadedness. Left after 15 minutes.

documents.title: Appointment cancelled

documents.body: Pt called, finals run through the 19th and she won't be home in time. Moved physical to 12/31 at 10:00.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Juniper, 20, home on winter break, here for her yearly exam.

Interval: one faint in May (ER, normal ECG, reflex pattern), seen here in June with normal labs. No further faints or near-faints since. Got through the fall choir concert on the risers using the tips we discussed. Flu and COVID done in October.

Meds: none. Allergies: none to drugs. Family history unchanged.
Social: still never smoked, no alcohol. Says the semester was stressful but finished well. Sleep okay most nights.
ROS: no chest pain, palpitations, exertional symptoms, headaches or GI complaints. Periods regular.

Exam: well. Vitals in flowsheet, normal. Eyes, ears and throat unremarkable. Thyroid normal size, no nodes. Heart regular without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft and nontender. Skin without rashes. Neuro normal. PHQ-2 is 1, no concerns raised.

Assessment and plan:
1. Preventive: up to date on vaccines. No labs needed this year. Cervical screening starts after she turns 21; we'll start it at next year's exam.
2. Syncope, one episode in May, none since: keep using the prevention steps. Same return precautions.

See her next winter break or sooner as needed.
